title: Evidence Before Entry
youtube_title: Evidence Before Entry: Why No Trade Can Be the Right Decision
instagram_caption: A paper-trading process is not about forcing a trade. It is about checking completed bars, fresh quotes, liquidity, and intraday confirmation before any order. If evidence is incomplete, standing down is a valid decision. scenes.title: A signal is not an order
scenes.narration: A setup score is only a starting point. It is not a filled order, and it is not a reason to trade by itself.

scenes.title: Use completed data
scenes.narration: Begin with completed, timestamped bars. Incomplete candles can change the picture while you are still measuring it.

scenes.title: Check the source
scenes.narration: Then confirm the quote is fresh, the market source is known, and the spread is narrow enough for the setup to be meaningful.

scenes.title: Look for missing evidence
scenes.narration: Missing history, stale data, wide spreads, or a broken sequence of rising closes are not small details. They are reasons to stop.

scenes.title: Respect the risk limit
scenes.narration: Even when a setup looks attractive, the position must fit the risk budget. If one unit is too large, the correct size can be zero.

scenes.title: No trade is a decision
scenes.overlay: Stand down when evidence is incomplete
scenes.narration: A disciplined process does not force a trade to meet a schedule. When the evidence is incomplete, standing down is the decision.
